what_the_writer_read:
Threat:
- ThreatFox, about the indicator only: 198.51.100.77:8443 (ip:port) is listed as win.nanocore, threat type botnet command and control.
- Background not evidence: NanoCore RAT: Windows remote-access trojan. The victim connects out to an operator-chosen host and port and speaks NanoCore's own protocol: length-prefixed, DES-encrypted frames over plain TCP. That channel carries no TLS handshake and never uses UDP.
- the flagged address 198.51.100.77 is in AS64510 Example VPS B.V. (NL).
Host:
- the address appears on 35 day(s) of campus history from 2026-10-21 to 2026-11-24, with traffic to or from a known remote address on 35.
- none of the products with a known purpose appears on its days of campus history.
- on 2026-11-22 it used 10 distinct services (the campus median was 13 and the 90th percentile 22) and moved 9.2 MB.
- names it used on the most of the 4 day(s) read, with the number of days: juniper-cloud.test (4), notify-hub.test (4), chalk-video.test (3), comet-games.test (3), drift-books.test (3), ember-code.test (3), ember-docs.test (3), hazel-health.test (3).
What happened:
- The host's contact with the flagged address: 198.51.100.77 8443/TCP, no name, 132 minute(s) on 2026-11-22..2026-11-24, first 2026-11-22 06:00 UTC, last 2026-11-24 23:30 UTC; 34.3 KB received, 55.2 KB sent.
- 198.51.100.77 carried at most 0 registered domain(s): not shown to be shared.
- From 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-24 (4 day(s)): after the first match the next destination new to this host was harbor-anchor-code.test, 13.6 h later; 3 new named destination(s) (this address used 10 distinct services on 2026-11-22, against a campus median of 13) and 1 network(s) with no name in all; uploads of 1 MB or more to new destinations: none.
Outcome:
- Outcome: review. We kept this case for review because: a scheduled low-volume contact.
- 3 finding(s); the first: scheduled low-volume contact with 198.51.100.77 on 2026-11-22: 36 minutes, mean gap 30.0 min, over 17.5 h.
- No ordinary reason found: 1 address, port and name combination(s) with 198.51.100.77 (no TLS name, so no site can be named). In detail: no TLS name: the contact cannot be attributed to a site.
Next steps:
- Identify the device: the address lease (DHCP, network access control or VPN logs) for HOST from 2026-11-22 05:45 UTC to 2026-11-23 00:30 UTC, and on the later match day(s) 2026-11-23..2026-11-24. An address is not a device.
- Find which process makes the scheduled contact; a schedule this regular is a program, not a person.
- Identify the process behind contact 198.51.100.77 8443/TCP, no name at 2026-11-22 06:00 UTC.
- Check the host's endpoint record for a NanoCore client process and its persistence (a .NET executable started from the user profile) and for outbound TCP from it.

paragraphs.summary: We found that ThreatFox lists 198.51.100.77:8443 as win.nanocore, a botnet command-and-control indicator. The device at 10.30.1.33 reached that address from 22 Nov 2026 06:00 UTC to 24 Nov 2026 23:30 UTC. We kept the case for review because a scheduled low-volume contact has no ordinary reason we can find. The next step is to identify the device from its address lease and check its endpoint record for the contact.
paragraphs.threat: ThreatFox lists 198.51.100.77:8443 as win.nanocore with the threat type botnet command and control. NanoCore is a Windows remote-access trojan: the victim connects out to an operator-chosen host and port and speaks its own length-prefixed, DES-encrypted protocol over plain TCP, without a TLS handshake.
paragraphs.host: From 21 Oct 2026 to 24 Nov 2026 the device at 10.30.1.33 was active on 35 days, all with traffic to or from a known remote address. On 22 Nov 2026 it used 10 distinct services and moved 9.2 MB. None of the products with a known purpose appears on its days, so we can only name the names it used most, such as juniper-cloud.test and notify-hub.test.
paragraphs.contact: The device at 10.30.1.33 contacted 198.51.100.77 on port 8443/TCP with no TLS name, for 132 minutes across 22 to 24 Nov 2026, first at 06:00 UTC on 22 Nov and last at 23:30 UTC on 24 Nov. It received 34.3 KB and sent 55.2 KB. The address carried no registered domains, so we cannot show it is shared.
paragraphs.why: We kept the case for review because the contact recurs on a schedule: 36 minutes on 22 Nov with a mean gap of 30.0 minutes over 17.5 hours. We found no ordinary reason, since the contact has no TLS name and so cannot be tied to any site.
paragraphs.after: From 21 Nov to 24 Nov 2026 the device reached 3 new named destinations after the first match, the first being harbor-anchor-code.test 13.6 hours later, and one network with no name. On 22 Nov 2026 alone it used 10 services, against a campus median of 13. We found no uploads of 1 MB or more to new destinations.
paragraphs.conclusion: We can say that the device at 10.30.1.33 made a scheduled, low-volume contact with 198.51.100.77:8443 over three days and that ThreatFox lists that address as a NanoCore indicator. We cannot say which program made the contact or what the device is, because an address is not a device and the contact has no TLS name. The next steps are to identify the device from its DHCP, network access control or VPN lease for 22 Nov 2026 05:45 UTC to 23 Nov 2026 00:30 UTC and the later match days; find the process behind the scheduled contact at 22 Nov 2026 06:00 UTC; and check the endpoint record for a NanoCore client and its persistence and outbound TCP.
